newsitem.title: USA: John Nuveen & Co hires three investment bankers.
newsitem.headline: John Nuveen & Co hires three investment bankers.

text.p: John Nuveen & Co Inc, wholly owned subsidiary of The John Nuveen Co, announced Thursday that Don Backstrom, Mark J. Laubacher and Timothy D. Wilschetz have joined the company as vice presidents in the Investment Banking Group.
"The creation of these three new positions is a result of Nuveen's expanding corporate and municipal finance business," said Clifton L. Fenton, Manager of Nuveen's Investment Banking Division.

"At a time when some other firms are downsizing or getting out of the business completely, Nuveen is increasing its commitment to providing investment banking services," Fenton said. "We are extremely pleased to be adding three very capable and experienced investment bankers to our growing team."

Backstrom is concentrating on transportation, local water agencies and general municipal issuers. From 1991 to 1997 Backstrom was a Vice President, Public Finance, at Smith Barney Inc. At Smith Barney he was responsible for originating public finance business in California.

Mark J. Laubacher joins Nuveen after 12 years with Bear, Stearns & Co., where he went from analyst to associate director. In his new role he will be responsible for state and large city issuers in the Midwest as well as Midwest state housing agencies.

Timothy D. Wilschetz is focusing on providing investment banking services to the transportation and utility industries and on developing Nuveen's presence in the U.S. infrastructure privatization markets. Prior to joining Nuveen, Wilschetz was a vice president, Project Finance and Privatization, with Cambridge Partners, L.L.C., an investment banking firm established in 1995.
Founded in 1898 and headquartered in Chicago, Nuveen specializes in providing municipal and corporate investment banking services and offers investment products.
